scope: Simulation reference tracking of original trained policies, with deployed target clipping. Legacy disabled-body-hull and corrected-contact cases remain separate. No hardware, thermal or policy hand-off validation.

recommendation.sit_stay_shake: Continue original policy for1000 additional iterations with corrected tracking ground hulls and deployment target clipping; preserve motion/reward/seed, then repeat this suite.
recommendation.spider_clips: Continue original policy for1000 additional iterations with corrected tracking ground hulls and deployment target clipping; preserve motion/reward/seed before considering reward changes.
recommendation.generated_trick: Selected sample03 passed the corrected-contact/clamp open-loop screen; train with corrected hulls, target clipping and preserved COM randomization.

interpretation: The course WOBBLES threshold is root tracking error>3cm or orientation error>10degrees. FALLS is a tracking label at>10cm or>45degrees, not a physical toppling detector.
The sitting reference intentionally tilts the torso. Absolute tilt around38degrees in sit is not evidence of a fall; compare reference orientation and contacts.
Approximate hull penetration samples mesh vertices and is not an exact convex-hull certificate. Soft contacts allow small penetration in corrected simulation.

Old v1 COM tests were erased by inertial randomization and are superseded. v2 explicitly reordered COM after inertia and verified actual offsets. v3 preserves RNG draws while retaining sampled COM; random seeds therefore should not be interpreted as exactly matched physical samples against v2.
Course tracking labels are not a complete behavior test: compare intended paw offer, stance joints, return-to-stand residuals, actual tilt, contacts and clearance separately.

Corrected lower-leg hulls can support the floor alongside foot balls. Their contact friction is1.0 against the course terrain while foot-ball friction is randomized; these tests vary foot material, not a uniformly slippery surface.
